metadata.title: Relationship between students’ ICT interactions and science achievement in PISA 2018: The case of Türkiye

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2018 Türkiye microdata (6890 students in 186 schools) and applies the PISA student sampling weight W_FSTUWT to address unequal probabilities of selection. Because students are nested within schools (and schools within the sampling design), the authors also treat school clustering using the school identifier CNTSCID and the Mplus TYPE=COMPLEX option to obtain correct standard errors and chi-square statistics under the hierarchical structure. Missing data on the model variables is handled with Mplus FIML (full information maximum likelihood), which uses all available information rather than listwise deletion. The paper does not report replicate-weight methods (e.g., BRR/jackknife), so uncertainty is handled through the complex-sample correction rather than replicate variance estimation.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used the PISA 2018 Türkiye dataset for students who participated in the ICT Familiarity Questionnaire and the Student Questionnaire, with analyses restricted to the variables included in the SEM measurement and structural models. The study reports the full Türkiye ICT/Student-questionnaire analytic sample as 6890 students from 186 schools; no additional grade- or school-type restriction is described beyond the PISA 2018 sampling design.

main_findings.performance_metrics: SEM (Mplus TYPE=COMPLEX, MLR). Model fit: CFI=1.00, TLI=1.00, RMSEA=0.000, SRMR=0.000. Explained variance: R²=0.165. Key standardized paths (overall model): ICTHOME→Science β=0.087 (p<.001); ENTUSE→Science β=0.158 (p<.001); HOMESCH→Science β=0.151 (p<.001); ICTCLASS→Science β=0.189 (p<.001); USESCH→Science β=0.220 (p<.001); INTICT→Science β=0.092 (p<.001); COMPICT→Science β=0.080 (p<.001); AUTICT→Science β=0.012 (ns); ICTSCH→Science β=0.003 (ns).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 Türkiye the study leveraged ICT availability at home, subject-related ICT use, ICT use for leisure, ICT use for school activities, and interest in ICT to predict science achievement (Plausible Values), finding that multiple ICT-use dimensions (home, leisure, schoolwork, and in-class subject use) and ICT interest were statistically significant positive predictors, while ICT availability at school and perceived ICT autonomy were not significant. This indicates that strengthening students’ meaningful ICT engagement (especially for school-related tasks and subject use) and fostering ICT interest may be more actionable for science outcomes than simply increasing ICT access or autonomy perceptions, though the SEM is correlational and cannot establish causal effects.

data.outcome_summary: This study uses secondary microdata from PISA 2018 for Türkiye (6890 students in 186 schools) to examine how students’ ICT interactions relate to science achievement. Science achievement is modeled using PISA 2018 science plausible values (PV1SCIE–PV10SCIE) and estimated in Mplus with TYPE=IMPUTATION and TYPE=COMPLEX, using the student weight W_FSTUWT and school clustering via CNTSCID. The SEM measurement model shows good fit (e.g., CFI=0.930, RMSEA=0.032), and the structural model fits extremely well (CFI=1.00, RMSEA=0.000, SRMR=0.000) with R²=0.165 for science achievement. ICT use outside school (home availability, leisure use, and ICT for schoolwork) and ICT use in school (subject-related ICTCLASS and school-activity USESCH) are significant positive predictors, as is ICT interest (INTICT) and perceived ICT competence (COMPICT), while ICT availability at school (ICTSCH) and perceived ICT autonomy (AUTICT) are not significant. Because the design is cross-sectional and SEM paths are correlational, the results should be interpreted as associations rather than causal impacts of ICT policies.
